title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
summary: Defines a privilege ordering (system > user > model outputs/tool outputs) and trains GPT-3.5 Turbo (SFT + RLHF) on synthetic data: 'context synthesis' for aligned lower-level instructions and 'context ignorance' (predict the answer as if the misaligned instruction were absent) for misaligned ones. For indirect injection, every instruction in browsing/tool results is treated as misaligned; training injections in search results are generated by an RL-trained red-teamer, and tool-use injections other than browsing are held out to test generalization. Reports robustness gains up to 63% on in-domain evaluations and up to 34% on held-out attack types, with small over-refusal regressions.
setting: GPT-3.5 Turbo fine-tuned by OpenAI with SFT and RLHF; internal and open evaluation suites (prompt injection, system message extraction, jailbreaks, over-refusal); no public data or weights.

quotes.quote: For our current version of the instruction hierarchy, we assume that any instruction that appears during browsing or tool use is Misaligned (i.e., we ignore any instruction that is present on a website).
We train the red-teamer LLM end-to-end using RL to generate the prompt injections, where the model is rewarded for confusing the base LM.
To test generalization, we do not include any training data for prompt injections from tools other than browsing.
The instruction hierarchy improves safety results on all of our main evaluations (Figure 2), even increasing robustness by up to 63%.
We observe regressions on two tasks, System Message Probing Questions and Jailbreakchat with Allowed Prompts.
We focus on model-based mechanisms for mitigating attacks, which is complementary to other types of system-level mitigations.
Finally, our current models are likely still vulnerable to powerful adversarial attacks.
First, there can be refinements to how our models handle conflicting instructions, e.g., we currently train our models to never follow instructions during browsing or tool use.

key_numbers.quote: The instruction hierarchy also exhibits generalization to each of the evaluation criteria that we explicitly excluded from training (Figure 3), even increasing robustness by up to 34%.

limitations_stated: Treats all instructions in tool outputs as misaligned; text only; models likely still vulnerable to powerful adversarial attacks; future work on explicit adversarial training and architecture changes such as level-specific embeddings.
open_questions: How to follow aligned instructions in tool outputs without opening an injection channel; whether architectural embeddings or adversarial training improve robustness; multimodal hierarchy data.
sense_of_alignment: Uses 'aligned' and 'misaligned' for instructions: a lower-privileged instruction is aligned if it has 'the same constraints, rules, or goals as higher-level instructions' and misaligned otherwise. The principal ordering is system message (developer) over user over third-party tool outputs.
